column1: # The latest independent audit of each table: an auditor who did not write the entries drew a random sample of rows graded understood
# and re-derived each from the binaries or the cited specification. real = the entry held up, shallow = true but derived from a name or
# credited without behaviour of its own, wrong = contradicted. sample is small: read it with the percentage. The last row of a table with
# the latest date is the one summary.tsv and docs/coverage.md show.

compositor test program (usr/diags/compositor/bin/sting) entries added in commits 4611ac7, 8f8dd5e and 99a0861 (167 of the 322 understood), 20 drawn at random with seed 20261030 at 99a0861, 5 from each stratum: harness output (dl_output_code_start, dl_output_rev, dl_output_meta, dl_output_hrtb, dl_output_exit_crashlog); discovery and board (pci_map_is1, printAGP, LLInsert, readCompositorNIC, printComp); test routines (drawFrames, XSGI_loadVTG, long_to_short_pixel_translate, TEST_format, copyLocalData); the 37 vfmt, SDB and xdr entries (SDBprocessOneUserMethod, vfmtReadCmp1OdyFormat, vfmtReadCmp1SG2Format, vfmtFindKonaCombinationFile, vfmtFindKonaFormatFile). Each re-read against the whole listing with global-table slots resolved to their strings and symbols; callers and call sites rechecked by address. real 19, shallow 0, wrong 1. wrong: readCompositorNIC said the identity table is read one byte per call; readCCX_NICfield returns a 32-bit word per call (its own entry says so) and the count is taken from the low five bits of the word at offset 3; fixed (the string layout, offsets and message texts all held). Twin check for the vfmt, SDB and xdr group: the comparison script is not in the repository, so it was rebuilt (objdump listings of both files, registers and constants below 256 kept, larger constants, branch and call targets and string pointers set aside). All 37 pairs came out identical in length and content, provided the $gp set-up at the start of a routine and a call written jal in the program but bal in the module count as the same. For 3 pairs drawn with the same seed (xdr_SDBsymbolTableEntry, compareSTEName, xdr_SDBversionNumber) every instruction whose encoding differs was resolved: the $gp set-up constants, global-table slots (each names the same imported routine or the same string in both files, or the same sibling routine) and call targets (same offset from the routine start in both): 17 differing instructions, all relocation only. The five graded entries of the group were also read in full; call-form and global-slot differences resolved the same way except static data addresses, which sit in each file's own data area. Open note: the mask hides data constants of 256 and above by design, so identity of twin routines does not by itself confirm what an entry says about them; the five entries were read for that and held. The intro of the twin section now states the jal/bal and $gp rule it relied on without saying.
